newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan denies blocking HK Telecom bid.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan denies blocking HK Telecom bid.

text.p: Taiwan's Ministry of Transport and Communications on Friday denied Hong Kong media reports that it was blocking Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd from bidding for Taiwan mobile phone franchises.
"We are still reviewing the qualifications of all 42 applicants, including Hong Kong Telecommunications," a ministry official who declined to be named told Reuters by telephone.
"There are all kinds of rumours because it's very competitive," the official added.

Hong Kong newspapers said on Friday that a Taiwan telecom official was reported to have said Hongkong Telecom was being blocked in the bidding process because of its state shareholder base in mainland China, Taiwan's arch rival.
Hongkong Telecom officials said in Hong Kong they were seeking clarification from Taiwan authorities on the reports.

The Taiwan communications ministry official, asked about the issue of Beijing's partial control of Hongkong Telecom, said two other cabinet agencies -- the economics ministry and Mainland Affairs Council -- also had a say in the matter.
"This (China ownership issue) should not be a big issue," the official said. "So far we are still reviewing all applicants and have not blocked anyone from participating."
"The Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Mainland Affairs Council will review the matter in accordance with Taiwan's regulations," he added.

Hong Kong-listed CITIC Pacific Ltd, controlled by the communist Chinese government's main overseas trade and investment arm, China International Trust and Investment Corp, or CITIC, holds about eight percent of Hongkong Telecom.
Hongkong Telecom holds a 15 percent interest in Taiwan's Taishiu Telecom Corp, which is among 42 bidders for eight mobile telephone operating licences whose franchise will span all or part of Taiwan.
Taishiu is bidding for two separate licences to offer Personal Communications Services and GSM mobile telephony services in northern Taiwan.

Taiwan officials have said they would announce results of the high-stakes bidding process on January 4 but Taiwan media reports on Friday indicated that the telecom ministry may not announce final results and could delay the announcement.
